## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a final decision tomorrow, could we talk tonight? You deserve a way out, but it might help to think through things like your finances, notice period, and whether there’s another job or some leave option available. If the situation is harming your health or feels unsafe, please put your wellbeing first. I’m here to listen—no judgment.

## 2

I understand why some images can seem suspicious, especially when they come through edited or compressed media, but the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on a single photograph. We can observe ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon, see different stars from different parts of the world, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and use time zones and satellite technology that work because Earth is spherical. Photos from space are taken by many independent governments, universities, and private companies, and their observations agree with one another. It’s reasonable to question evidence, but the flat-Earth explanation would have to account for all of these observations—and it doesn’t.

## 3

The sky looks blue because sunlight is made of many colors, and Earth’s atmosphere is full of tiny gas molecules. When sunlight passes through the air, those molecules scatter the shorter blue and violet wavelengths much more strongly than the longer red and orange ones. Our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet, and some violet light is absorbed, so blue becomes the color we notice most. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more reds and oranges to reach our eyes.

雨落在深夜的城市里，像无数细小的手指，轻轻敲打着窗玻璃。路灯被水汽晕成温柔的光团，空荡的街道泛着一层银色，偶尔有汽车驶过，车轮溅起水花，又很快消失在巷口。屋檐下的风带着泥土和潮湿树叶的气味，远处传来模糊的雷声。房间里只有钟表的滴答声和雨声相伴，让人感到孤独，却也莫名安心。
